title: The Sandalwood Merchant and the Four Sharpers
summary: An honest merchant of Kashgar arrived in a foreign coastal city with a valuable caravan of rare sandalwood. He was met by four notorious sharpers who resolved to swindle him of ...
keywords: the sandal-wood merchant and the sharpers
full_text:
An honest merchant of Kashgar arrived in a foreign coastal city with a valuable caravan of rare sandalwood. He was met by four notorious sharpers who resolved to swindle him of his goods through fraudulent wagers and trickery.

The first sharper convinced him that his sandalwood was worthless firewood, offering a handful of copper for it. The second challenged him to a rigged game of dice; the third claimed the merchant had stolen his eye; and the fourth claimed the merchant had promised to drink up the sea!

Penniless and surrounded by corrupt lawsuits, the poor merchant sat weeping in an alley. An old blind woman passing by took pity on him: 'Go to the tavern of the blind shaykh outside the gate; every evening, all the sharpers of the city gather to boast of their tricks to him, and he analyzes their flaws!'

The merchant disguised himself in rags, entered the tavern, and listened from the shadows.

The four sharpers entered, bragging to the blind shaykh of how they had trapped the sandalwood merchant.

The blind shaykh laughed scornfully: 'You fools think you have won, but you have left yourselves open to ruin! If he demands that the sandalwood be weighed against pure gold, the first must pay; if he says to the second that he will play if the winner drinks all the sea, he must demand that the ocean’s rivers be dammed first; and if he agrees to give an eye to the third, he must demand that both their eyes be plucked and weighed upon a balance to ensure an exact match!'

The merchant memorized the advice, appeared before the city magistrate the next morning, and turned the sharpers’ own traps upon them with lightning wit!

The terrified sharpers paid the merchant ten thousand dinars to withdraw the suits, and the merchant returned home in triumph, having learned that wise counsel conquers the sharpest fraud.
moral: When surrounded by deceitful adversaries in a strange city, seek the counsel of the wise elder.
